fleetMemoryScratch: LESSON: src/lib/parcel-record-engine/*.js in hauska-factory is vendored from hauska-engine (packages/engine-core/src/parcel-record), pinned by ENGINE_PIN.json, and explicitly hand-edit-forbidden. A new rail derivation that needs no new engine semantics (pure countyFips/static-config logic, or mirroring a sibling cell's already-resolved state) belongs at the JOB layer in the consuming job file, not the engine -- ingestJurisdictionOntoRecords (cityLimits) is the established precedent; this lane added three more (situsState, acreageSqft, landUseVintage) on the same pattern.

LESSON: a rail with zero earned cells anywhere is 'declared-ahead' and excluded from the publish gate (liveness.js's deriveLiveRailKeys); the moment even one cell earns a real state, the rail becomes LIVE and every remaining unaccounted cell on it, program-wide, starts gating. Landing even a small, correct fix flips this switch -- converging the fix close to completion (via a real fill-job run) matters more for rails that start at 100% unaccounted than for one already partially live.

LESSON: parcel-record-fill.mjs and parcel-r5-zoning.mjs both hard-refuse --apply outside Cloud Run (LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN, checked against env.FACTORY_CLOUD==='1') -- a lane working from a non-Cloud-Run environment can verify everything (unit tests, --sample/dry-run pilots against live read-only data) except the actual production write, which can only happen by triggering the real Cloud Run job execution.

LESSON: cad_property.exemption_codes is text[]; the array-handling fix landed 2026-09-05 (ENGINE_PIN dfdf6fd, PR #381) but a pin landing in the codebase does not retroactively fix rows a --apply run already wrote under the OLD code -- those rows need a re-run, and 'the code is right but the data is stale' is a genuinely different diagnosis from 'the write path is vacuous', distinguishable only by replaying the CURRENT code against the SAME stuck rows and checking whether it resolves them.
